pharm: Butyrophenone antipsychotic; decanoate ester for prolonged IM depot release
quick: Deep IM: ~10-20x the previous daily oral haloperidol dose monthly; initial usually <=100 mg, then titrate (often up to ~50-200 mg q4 weeks; max 300 mg/month)
Risk of extrapyramidal/withdrawal symptoms in neonates with 3rd-trimester exposure; use only if benefit justifies risk
Excreted in breast milk; monitor infant for sedation/EPS, generally avoid
Use with caution; no specific depot adjustment established
Use with caution; metabolized hepatically - reduce/avoid in significant impairment
ECG/QTc, EPS, tardive dyskinesia, electrolytes (K/Mg), CBC, signs of NMS
summary: Haloperidol decanoate is the long-acting depot ester of haloperidol given by deep IM injection (usually monthly) for maintenance treatment of schizophrenia in patients requiring prolonged parenteral antipsychotic therapy. Patients should first be stabilized on, and tolerate, oral haloperidol. Carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.
indications: Treatment of patients with schizophrenia who require prolonged parenteral antipsychotic therapy

dosage.c: Schizophrenia maintenance (adult, stabilized on oral haloperidol)
dosage.d: Initial monthly dose ~10-20x the previous daily oral haloperidol dose
dosage.t: Usually administered every 4 weeks; titrate per response
dosage.n: Initial dose generally not to exceed 100 mg; max volume per injection site 3 mL; do NOT give IV
Supplement with oral haloperidol during initial conversion period as needed

admin: Administer by DEEP intramuscular injection only - DO NOT give intravenously
Use a 21-gauge needle; maximum 3 mL per injection site
Patient must be stabilized on and tolerate short-acting (oral) haloperidol before conversion
Inspect visually for particulate matter/discoloration before use
Close clinical supervision required during the initial conversion period
moa: Haloperidol is a butyrophenone antipsychotic that acts primarily as an antagonist at central dopamine D2 receptors; the precise mechanism in schizophrenia is unclear but is thought to be mediated by postsynaptic dopamine receptor blockade. The decanoate ester provides slow release from the IM depot, prolonging the duration of action.

absolute: Severe toxic CNS depression or comatose states from any cause
relative: QT prolongation / hypokalemia / hypomagnesemia / known cardiac disease
History of seizures or EEG abnormalities
Concomitant QT-prolonging or strongly sedating drugs

preg: Neonates exposed to antipsychotics in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms after delivery. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Haloperidol is excreted in human breast milk; infants should be monitored for sedation and extrapyramidal symptoms. Breastfeeding generally not recommended with depot therapy.
renal: Use with caution; no specific depot dose adjustment is established. The long-acting nature complicates dose modification.
hepatic: Haloperidol is extensively metabolized by the liver; use with caution and consider dose reduction or avoidance in significant hepatic impairment.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, methadone, certain antibiotics/antifungals) - additive QT/Torsades risk
moderate: Carbamazepine, rifampin (enzyme inducers reduce haloperidol levels)
Anticholinergics (additive effects, may worsen tardive dyskinesia)
interactions.diagnostics: Baseline and periodic ECG (QTc); electrolytes (potassium, magnesium); CBC

serious: QTc prolongation / Torsades de Pointes / sudden death
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, altered mental status)

monitoring: Serum potassium and magnesium (correct before/during therapy)
Extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia (e.g., AIMS)
CBC (especially first months in those with low/falling WBC)
Signs of NMS; mental status and clinical response
counsel: This is a long-acting injection given about once a month
Report fever with muscle stiffness, fainting, palpitations, or uncontrolled movements promptly
Avoid alcohol and other sedating substances
May cause drowsiness - use caution with driving/machinery
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness from low blood pressure
pk: Delayed (depot); therapeutic effect builds over days to weeks
Plasma concentration peaks ~3-9 days after IM injection
Protect from light; do not freeze; store per label (room temperature)
pearls: Boxed warning: elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotics have increased mortality; haloperidol decanoate is NOT approved for this use.
Never give IV - associated with QT prolongation and Torsades; depot is for deep IM use only.
Always stabilize and confirm tolerance on oral haloperidol before converting to the decanoate depot.
Because steady state takes ~2-3 months, oral supplementation may be needed during initial conversion.
missed: Depot injections are clinician-administered; if a scheduled monthly dose is delayed, contact the prescriber to reschedule and assess whether interim oral antipsychotic cover is needed. Do not double the depot dose.
overdose: Manifestations include severe extrapyramidal reactions, hypotension, sedation, and QT prolongation/arrhythmias. Management is supportive (airway, cardiac monitoring); treat dystonia with anticholinergics, hypotension with fluids/pressors (avoid epinephrine due to possible paradoxical hypotension). The depot prolongs the duration of toxicity.
